title: Your best AX fixes are hiding in agent trajectories
summary:
All five agent runs produced a working script, and nothing in the eval score looked wrong. The trajectories told a different story. Every run read a DLL as raw bytes to find plugin names, and three scripts would quietly reroute a CI runner's network traffic. Here are the patterns to look for in your own agents' trajectories, and what to change in your product when you find them.

The post Your best AX fixes are hiding in agent trajectories appeared first on Microsoft for Developers.

title: Does ‘eval’ in the workspace path change what your agent does?
summary:
Your eval might be telling the agent it’s a test before the agent reads a single instruction. Eval tools need a fresh folder for every run, and the easiest way to get one is a temp directory with a random name like /tmp/eval-7f3a2c. The agent sees that path on every turn, in the system prompt […]
